title: Basic Pancakes
text:
!! About

Few foods carry as much quiet joy as a stack of pancakes. Golden, tender, faintly crisp at the edges and pillowy at the center, they manage to feel simultaneously humble and celebratory — the kind of thing that turns an ordinary Tuesday morning into something worth getting out of bed for. A drizzle of maple syrup, a pat of butter melting into the top, the faint steam rising from the plate: pancakes don't ask much of you, and in return they give a great deal.

The pancake is ancient. Versions of it appear in nearly every food culture on earth — the French crêpe, the Russian blini, the Ethiopian injera, the Japanese okonomiyaki. The basic idea is nearly as old as cooking itself: grain ground to flour, mixed with liquid, cooked on a hot flat surface. Roman writings mention a thin wheat cake sweetened with honey; Ötzi the Iceman, the 5,300-year-old glacier mummy, had einkorn wheat in his stomach that may well have been eaten as a kind of flatcake. Shrove Tuesday (Pancake Day) in Britain has been a reason to cook them since at least the 15th century, a way to use up butter and eggs before the Lenten fast.

The American breakfast pancake — thick, leavened with baking powder, eaten in stacks — is a more recent invention, a product of the 19th century when chemical leaveners became widely available. But it adapted quickly into a beloved ritual: lazy weekend mornings, diner counters, school fundraisers. This recipe is that classic version, straightforward enough to make from memory once you've done it a few times, reliable enough to anchor the morning every time.

!! Ingredients

* 1 cup [[flour]]
* 2 teaspoons [[baking powder]]
* 1 tablespoon [[sugar]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[salt]]
* 1 cup [[milk]]
* 1 [[egg]]
* 2 tablespoons [[butter]], melted

!! Steps

# Whisk together the [[flour]], [[baking powder]], [[sugar]], and [[salt]] in a large bowl.
# In a separate bowl, combine the [[milk]], [[egg]], and melted [[butter]].
# Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine.
# Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat.
# Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake onto the skillet.
# Cook until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set, about 2 minutes.
# Flip and cook for another 1–2 minutes until golden brown.
# Serve hot with toppings of your choice.
